'''Julia Gordon''' is a Canadian mathematician at the [[University of British Columbia]] whose research concerns [[algebraic geometry]], including [[representation theory]], [[p-adic number|{{mvar|p}}-adic groups]], [[motivic integration]], and the [[Langlands program]].

Gordon earned her PhD at the [[University of Michigan]] in 2003 under the supervision of [[Thomas Callister Hales|Thomas C. Hales]] and [[Robert Griess]]. Her dissertation was ''Some Applications of Motivic Integration to the Representation Theory of P-adic Groups''.{{r|mgp}} After postdoctoral research at the [[University of Toronto]] and the [[Fields Institute]], she joined the University of British Columbia faculty in 2006. {{As of|2021}}, she is an associate professor there.{{r|rm|kn}} In 2026, Gordon is listed as an associate professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=UBC |url=https://m.directory.ubc.ca/index.cfm?detail=1000010728 |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=m.directory.ubc.ca}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2017, Gordon won the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|rm}}She served her Michler Fellowship at [[Cornell University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julia Gordon {{!}} Department of Mathematics |url=https://math.cornell.edu/julia-gordon |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=math.cornell.edu |language=en}}</ref>
She is the 2019 winner of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].{{r|kn}}
